_comment: FIN-002 monthly cost ceilings per environment, in USD, compared against an Infracost breakdown's projects[].breakdown.totalMonthlyCost. THIS FILE IS THE ENFORCED SOURCE: run.sh passes `--data policy` on every conftest invocation, which exposes the top-level keys below as data.dev / data.prod, and policy/finops.rego reads them through STATIC references (data.dev, data.prod) - a dynamic data[env] is a compile error inside package main. `opa test policy tests` loads this file as data the same way, so the unit tests read the same numbers CI enforces. finops.rego also carries fin002_embedded_budget so that a bare `conftest test` with no --data flag still enforces something; that copy is NOT trusted to stay in sync by hand - tests/finops_test.rego::test_fin002_embedded_budget_matches_budget_json asserts it equals this file value-for-value and fails the gate if it drifts. Adding an environment requires BOTH a key here and a matching static clause in fin002_budget_max; the same test is what catches doing only one. Values are written with a decimal point on purpose: sprintf's %f verb refuses an int64, so a bare 625 would render as '%!f(int64=625)' - finops.rego's fin002_usd helper defends against that too, and has a unit test for the integer case. DERIVATION (2026-08-27, from real Infracost v0.10.45 breakdowns of the vendored root module - see the _provenance block in each fixture): dev single-NAT measured 594.416, dev per-AZ-NAT measured 660.116, prod measured 853.404. dev=625.0 sits near the midpoint of (594.416, 660.116): the shipped single-NAT topology passes with 5.1% headroom and the per-AZ topology is refused with 5.3% margin, so neither verdict flips on ordinary price drift - a ceiling one percent above its own baseline turns the build red for a non-reason, and one percent below the violating case makes the negative control the fragile one instead. prod=900.0 is measured 853.404 plus 5.5% headroom; the number is unchanged from the earlier placeholder but is now derived rather than guessed. These are ceilings over point-in-time estimates, not statements about what anything costs now.
